newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moldova-Dnestr memorandum to be signed on May 8.
newsitem.headline: Moldova-Dnestr memorandum to be signed on May 8.

text.p: Leaders of Moldova and its separatist Dnestr region will sign a memorandum on Thursday to normalise ties in the former Soviet republic, Russian President Boris Yeltsin's spokesman said on Monday.

Sergei Yastrzhembsky told reporters that representatives of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), Russia and Ukraine would also take part in the signing ceremony in Moscow. He gave no further details.
Moldova and its separatist region made a breakthrough during talks in April, resolving differences which had held up the signing of the memorandum for months.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, who mediated in talks between President Petru Lucinschi and Dnestr separatist leader Igor Smirnov, had said the memorandum would be signed by May 15.
An agreement setting out terms for normalising ties, shattered by clashes over Dnestr's independence in 1992, was worked out last summer.
But Lucinschi had said he would only sign it if it was altered to respect Moldova's territorial integrity.

Since then, an article committing both sides to "relations within the framework of a common state and within the framework of (the former) Moldovian Soviet Socialist Republic's borders as of January 1990" has been added.
Primakov said this article had removed the obstacles to the memorandum, explaining that January 1990 preceded Dnestr's declaration of independence.
The two sides would start work on a document defining the status of the Dnestr region within the Republic of Moldova after the memorandum is signed.

Security forces of Moldova, where most people speak a Latin language related to that of neighbouring Romania, clashed in 1992 with separatists demanding independence for the Russian and Ukrainian-speaking people of Dnestr, an eastern region which is the country's industrial heartland.
Hundreds of people were killed before Russian peacekeeping troops intervened.
Russia still has up to 6,000 peacekeepers in Dnestr, a region with a population of about 700,000.
